note: Contract §11.5.3: the closed table an NPC's standing action in a fight is read from. A disposition is how this person behaves in a fight; its rows are tried in order and the first row whose every `when` condition holds gives the action. The last row of each disposition has no `when`, so every disposition gives an action. Conditions: `hp_fraction_at_most` (the participant's hp_current / hp_max in the saved combat snapshot is at most this number), `outnumbered` (true: more opponents who can still fight than people on the NPC's own side who can, the NPC included), `stance_in` (the NPC's stance word from the ledger, §17.3, is one of these). Every number lives here; the kernel writes no threshold of its own. Actions: attack (the clerk binds the attack), hold (does not attack this round: holds back, yields or surrenders, which the Keeper narrates), flee (tries to get away, which the Keeper narrates; the engine has no NPC flee action).

fights_to_the_end.description: Fights on whatever it costs: never breaks off, never yields.

fights_then_flees.description: Fights while the fight goes its way; runs once badly hurt, or once hurt and outnumbered. Does not strike first at someone it is not hostile to.

avoids_fighting.description: Does not want this fight: gets away when outnumbered or hurt, otherwise holds back rather than strike.

surrenders.description: Fights only while unhurt and not outnumbered; yields as soon as the fight turns against it.

tactic_note: Contract §11.5.3, amendment 2026-09-24 (SL-19): the disposition a person's stated tactic reads as, when they have no disposition. Only a tactic someone stated counts -- the book's (the record's combat.defense) or the Keeper's (apply npc defense) -- never the rules default from Fighting and Dodge. It is the rules default of the clerk's disposition bind when Jev does not settle one. Keys are the defence words (dodge, fight_back, none), values the four dispositions; a defence word without a row gives no default.
